text:
B: Alright! Hello, hello. Can you hear me?
A: Yeah, hiya. Sorry, I'm Jodie. You're the sparky, aren't you?
B: Ha, is it the polo? Tendai. Yeah, electrician, in Gloucester. Everybody knows straight away.
A: My boyfriend's a sparky, so I clocked it. Ryan. And the lady I just had, her fella's one as well. We're surrounded.
B: Leanne! With the switch hanging off the wall. Yeah, I had her first. She's funny, man.
A: She told me I say bap wrong. I don't. Erm, do you know what this pays, by the way? I keep asking and nobody knows.
B: Ha, no idea. A voucher? I'm just enjoying sitting down, you know. Fifty hours this week. So you're the student, yeah?
A: Yeah. MA in UX design, in Birmingham. I'm from Walsall. I used to do banners at a print place but it was dead end, so I've gone back to retrain. For the money, honestly.
B: Nothing wrong with that. I went self-employed for the money. People say passion, I say mortgage.
A: Exactly! That's what I keep saying. Leanne thinks UX is just buttons.
B: Buttons? Everything's buttons now. My mum in Harare, I set her up on WhatsApp, she rings me because she can't find the button to send a photo. So somebody needs to fix that, yeah? That's you.
A: See, that's literally it. That's the job. You get it more than my nan does.
B: Ha! Is Ryan on early starts?
A: Always. He's gone by half six, I'm still asleep. Then I'm up till two doing coursework in a panic, so we basically live in shifts.
B: Ah, that's like me and Natalie. She's a dental nurse, I'm out early, we see each other at dinner and then I'm asleep on the sofa by nine.
A: Ryan does that! Mouth open, football on. He's Wolves, so it's usually miserable.
B: Wolves, oh no. Tell him an Arsenal man feels for him. A little bit.
A: He'll love that. Erm, have you got kids?
B: Natalie's boy, Kai, thirteen. He's mine really. Been there since he was four. He eats everything, he grows out of boots every two months.
A: Aw. Ryan wants kids, like, sooner. I'm... not sure yet. Sorry, I don't know why I said that to a stranger.
B: No, it's fine, man. You've got time. I didn't plan anything, Kai just came with the package and now I can't imagine it. Everybody's different, you know.
A: Yeah. Anyway. I've got a cat, that's enough responsibility. She knocks everything off my desk.
B: I saw her! On the chair in your picture. Our house, no pets, just a van on the drive full of cable offcuts.
A: Ryan's van's the same. Receipts everywhere. I bake when I'm stressed and he eats it all in the van, there's crumbs in every crack.
B: You bake? What do you bake?
A: Brownies mostly. Cookies. I make loads and give it away, cause otherwise I'll eat it.
B: Ah, you need to come to my barbecue then. Half the street comes. Bring brownies, you're in.
A: Ha, deal. Is that the timer already? That went quick, sorry. Tara, then —
